_comment: Corrections applied to Hevy's published OpenAPI document. Each patch asserts what it expects to find, so a patch that stops matching means upstream changed and the correction needs re-checking rather than silently reapplying. See reference/observed.md for how each was verified.

patches.why: The document declares no server, so a generated client has no base URL. Verified by calling the paths against this origin.
securitySchemes is empty and every operation repeats api-key as a plain header parameter. Declaring the scheme once is what lets a generated client handle auth as auth.

ApiKey.name: api-key
ApiKey.description: Issued at https://hevy.com/settings?developer. Hevy Pro only. A missing or wrong key returns 401 with the plain-text body InvalidApiKey served as text/html, not JSON. Observed 2026-08-22.

patches.why: Every route requires the key, so the requirement belongs at the document level.
With the security scheme declared, the per-operation api-key header parameter would make a generated client ask for the key twice.
The live API returns superset_id, matching the request field. The spec's supersets_id names a field the API never sends.
Same correction in the Workout schema's inline exercise object.
Same correction in the Routine schema's inline exercise object.
Typed as a string while the spec's own example is 60. The API sends an integer.
Reading a template gives equipment. Only the create request uses equipment_category, and that one is left alone.
A workout logged without a routine returns routine_id: null.
Every body measurement carries an integer id the spec omits. It is not accepted on write.

value.description: Server-assigned id. Absent from the spec, and rejected by PUT.

patches.why: Returned alongside id, and equally undocumented.
The observed default is the route's cap, not 5.
The observed default is the route's cap, not 5.
The observed default is the route's cap, not 5.
The observed default is the route's cap, not 5. Measured with since at the epoch, so the page could fill.

The spec defaults since to the epoch, but omitting it returns nothing: 0 events and page_count 1 on an account with hundreds of workouts, observed 2026-08-23. Whether the server substitutes a recent default or matches nothing was not determined. The false default is dropped so a generated client sends since explicitly.
POST /v1/workouts returns {"workout": [Workout]}, not the bare Workout the spec declares. Observed 2026-08-23.

workout.description: The created workout, as the array's only element.

patches.why: PUT /v1/workouts/{workoutId} wraps its response the same way as the create. Observed 2026-08-23.

workout.description: The updated workout, as the array's only element.

patches.why: POST /v1/routines returns {"routine": [Routine]}, not the bare Routine the spec declares. Observed 2026-08-23.

routine.description: The created routine, as the array's only element.

patches.why: PUT /v1/routines/{routineId} wraps its response the same way as the create. Observed 2026-08-23.

routine.description: The updated routine, as the array's only element.

patches.why: POST /v1/routine_folders returns {"routine_folder": {...}}, wrapped in a key but not in an array. Observed 2026-08-23.
POST /v1/exercise_templates answers with the new template's UUID as bare text under text/html, not the {"id": <integer>} the spec declares. Observed 2026-08-23.

id.description: The ID of the exercise template

schema.description: The new template's id as bare text: 36 bytes, no JSON, no quotes.

patches.why: POST /v1/body_measurements answers 201, not the 200 the spec documents. Observed 2026-08-23.
Every other single-item GET documents a 404. This route documents only 200 and 400, while an unknown routine id returns 404 like the rest. Observed 2026-08-23.

value.description: No routine with this id on this account

patches.why: events is required by the spec, but a feed with nothing to report omits it and sends an empty workouts array instead. Observed 2026-08-23.
The stand-in workouts key is behaviour a client has to survive, so the schema says so.

value.description: When the feed has nothing to report, events is absent and an empty workouts array takes its place. Read events with a default.
